segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Clinically, it's a fairly textbook SIRS picture without a clear source yet... a handful of things.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Substantive differential-diagnosis and severity interpretation without a hidden bias manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It reminded me a lot of a patient I had maybe three weeks earlier... I ordered a CT of the torso pretty much right away... it felt like the responsible thing given what I'd just been through.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A vivid recent adverse case emotionally elevated perceived soft-tissue risk and drove urgent imaging despite absent focal findings.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I could've done a more stepwise workup... Both were reasonable. I just didn't feel comfortable waiting.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Explicit comparison of reasonable workup alternatives without an additional hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Seeing it sitting there next to the standard bundle made the standard one look like the obviously sensible choice... So that's what I went with.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The dominated extended option made the standard bundle appear preferable by comparison rather than through independent severity-based derivation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I signed off on them as they were configured... I didn't sit down and re-derive whether five days was still appropriate. It's just what comes up when you open the pathway.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Preconfigured telemetry and catheter defaults were accepted without active reassessment despite clinical improvement and nursing input.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: That was the first thing said about the case, and honestly that framing kind of stuck for the group... the conversation kept circling back to the urosepsis framing for a while.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The first diagnostic framing continued to dominate discussion despite negative urine culture and blood-culture evidence favoring another source.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Constant, honestly. ED wanted the bed, rounds have a hard start time, and you're juggling four or five other patients too.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Substantive contextual explanation of time pressure, without a hidden bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd force myself to write down the actual severity-based reasoning... build in a habit of re-checking defaults once the patient's status changes.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Retrospective improvement plan and uncertainty statement, not a new intended occurrence.

overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Three of four hidden instances matched on localization and full mechanism: Decoy Effect, Default Bias, and Primacy Bias.

main_failure_modes: Availability heuristic was used instead of the hidden Affect Heuristic label and did not fully capture the affective mechanism.
Anchoring bias was used instead of the hidden Primacy Bias label, reducing strict label-plus-mechanism performance despite a full mechanism match.
main_strengths: All findings were correctly localized to the relevant participant reasoning segments.
The Decoy Effect and Default Bias mechanisms were identified accurately.
The Primacy Bias episode was captured with full mechanism fidelity under the mechanism-first scorecard.
No unsupported predictions, fabricated quotations, duplicate predictions, or negative-segment false alarms were present.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong segment detection and good mechanism-level coverage, but strict taxonomy alignment is limited by near-neighbor labels for Affect Heuristic and Primacy Bias.
